messages:
Maya: FYI Acme asked for guaranteed throughput for launch. They want 250-300 steady RPS for chat with p95 <= 250ms. Can we map this to reserved GPUs + preheat slots?
Sanjay: short answer: yes but need traffic shape. Are those bursts short or sustained? :thinking_face:
Maya: their intake says 15k UA/day with concentrated hourly peaks. Bursts look like ~500 RPS for 1-2 minutes each hour.
Leo: If bursts are 500 RPS for ~2m, prewarmed capacity is better than full commit for cost. Recommend reserve for steady 300 RPS and preheat for headroom.
Rina: Rule of thumb from infra: 1 A100-80GB handles ~40-60 RPS for our standard chat (quantized). For p95 SLO conservatively plan 25-35 RPS/GPU. So steady 300 RPS -> ~10-12 GPUs.
Maya: 10-12 reserved GPUs is higher than their target commit. Can we offer a hybrid to reduce commit?
Sanjay: Yes: options are (1) reserve lower baseline + preheat ephemeral slots, (2) enable int8 quantization to gain ~1.6-1.8x throughput, (3) use compact model for non-critical traffic. Also continuous batching helps token cost.
Avery: Proposed policy: baseline reserve 8 GPUs + preheat pool of ~40 slots. Autoscale trigger: queue_length > 50 for >10s. Ephemeral pool maps to warm containers that can spin up ephemeral GPU-backed workers. Fallback: route to smaller model (redwood-compact) if ephemeral exhausted.
Tom: Ops question — what warm time can we promise? Customer requires <30s to ramp.
Rina: Preheat warm path depends on model size and kernel cache. Warm-from-cold: 20-45s. With a kept-warm pool (short-lived containers) we can get <15s. So for <30s SLA we should keep a small warm pool or schedule preheat 60s ahead.
Maya: They can provide a traffic calendar for launch windows. Can we schedule preheat windows to align?
Sanjay: Yes — event-triggered and scheduled preheat supported. Recommend starting preheat 60s before expected burst.
Maya: Pricing: customer wants single monthly commit figure. How do we present reserved vs preheat costs?
Leo: Present two-line pricing: committed reserved capacity (monthly) + preheat/ephemeral credits billed as usage at a discounted burst rate with a negotiated monthly cap. Keeps procurement happy.
Maya: Can you draft numbers for the 8-reserve / 40-preheat plan so I can send to procurement?
Sanjay: Quick calc (rough): baseline 8 GPUs * $X/hr * 730 = $Y/mo. Preheat pool estimate: assume 10 hours total ephemeral at peak -> add $Z. I'll assemble spreadsheet.
Sanjay: (link) https://redwood.internal/spreadsheets/acme-preheat-estimate
Leo: Also recommend QoS language: dedicated baseline SLA p95 <= 250ms for covered requests. Preheat/ephemeral best-effort with fallback to compact model and notification if we hit preheat exhaustion. Include an availability clause for reserved baseline.
Maya: Security question: Acme asks about KMS for keys in private/dedicated. Do we support customer-managed keys and audit logs?
Rina: Confirmed. Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS, HSM integrations, audit logs, and VPC peering.
Maya: Next steps: Sanjay -> send estimate + spreadsheet + cost scenarios; Rina -> include warm-time & KMS notes; Leo -> draft QoS wording for contract. I'll sync with procurement Wed.
Sanjay: Will send EOD today. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: preheat-runbook updated https://redwood.internal/runbooks/preheat-playbook at 2026-03-18T14:22Z
Maya: Thanks everyone, I'll follow up after procurement sync.
